title: Ecological Imbalances — Pollution and Climate Change
topicTitle: Ecological imbalances: greenhouse effects and climate change, depletion of ozone layer, acid rain and biological invasion

notes: Ecological imbalances: human-induced disruptions of natural ecosystems.
Greenhouse effect and climate change: greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, CFCs) trap heat → global warming; effects: melting ice, rising sea levels, extreme weather, habitat loss.
Ozone layer depletion: CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) destroy stratospheric ozone (O3) → increased UV radiation → skin cancer, cataracts, crop damage.
Acid rain: SO2 and NOx from industry + vehicles → H2SO4, HNO3 in rain → acidic rain (pH < 5.6) → damage to forests, aquatic ecosystems, buildings.
Biological invasion: non-native species introduced to new environments → outcompete native species → biodiversity loss; e.g., water hyacinth in Nepal.
Causes: deforestation, industrialisation, urbanisation, agriculture, overpopulation, pollution.
Effects: loss of biodiversity, ecosystem degradation, climate change, health problems.
Control measures: reduce emissions, plant trees, sustainable agriculture, international agreements (Kyoto, Paris), conservation of protected areas.
Nepal: vulnerable to climate change (Himalayan glaciers melting, flooding in Terai); air pollution in Kathmandu Valley (PM2.5 exceeds WHO limits).
NEB focus: greenhouse effect and climate change, ozone layer depletion, acid rain, and biological invasion.
confusion: The greenhouse effect is a NATURAL phenomenon (essential for life); the "enhanced" greenhouse effect (due to human emissions) causes climate change.
Ozone layer depletion (stratospheric O3 destroyed by CFCs) is different from the greenhouse effect (tropospheric gases trapping heat).
Acid rain is caused by SO2 and NOx (industry, vehicles), NOT by CO2 alone.
Biological invasion involves NON-NATIVE species; it is different from natural colonisation.
Climate change affects ecosystems at all scales (local to global).
Ozone (O3) is beneficial in the stratosphere (blocks UV) but harmful at ground level (air pollutant, smog).

universalFacts: Atmospheric CO2 has risen from ~280 ppm (pre-industrial) to ~420 ppm (2023).
Global average temperature has risen ~1.1°C since pre-industrial times.
The ozone hole over Antarctica reached its maximum in 2006 (~28 million km²).
Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) is an invasive species in Nepal's lakes and rivers, smothering aquatic life.
examples: Greenhouse effect: CO2 + CH4 + CFCs trap infrared radiation → warming.
Ozone depletion: CFCs (from refrigerators, aerosols) release Cl atoms → destroy O3 → increased UV → skin cancer.
Acid rain: SO2 (coal plants) + NOx (vehicles) → H2SO4, HNO3 in rain → acidic rain → forest damage, lake acidification.
Biological invasion: water hyacinth in Phewa Lake, Pokhara → smothered native fish and plants → oxygen depletion.
Control: tree planting, renewable energy, emission reduction, international agreements (Kyoto, Paris).

enrichedContent.summary: Human activities cause ecological imbalances: the enhanced greenhouse effect (CO2, CH4, CFCs) drives climate change; CFCs deplete the ozone layer, increasing UV radiation; SO2 and NOx cause acid rain (pH < 5.6); and biological invasions (e.g., water hyacinth in Nepal) threaten native biodiversity. These imbalances cause biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, and health problems. Control measures include reducing emissions, planting trees, sustainable agriculture, and international agreements (Kyoto, Paris). Nepal is particularly vulnerable to climate change (melting glaciers, Terai flooding) and air pollution (Kathmandu Valley PM2.5).
